subject: Orion Financial — access controls onboarding: SSO/SCIM/IP/service accounts
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@orionfin.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-07T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: SSO + SCIM + IP allowlist for Redwood integration

Hi Irene —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our security and identity teams reviewed the notes and want to start an access-controls onboarding plan so we can go live with Redwood in our staging environment next month. High-level asks:

- SSO via SAML (IdP: Okta) — we need assertion mapping and expected NameID/attributes.
- SCIM provisioning for groups and service accounts (we prefer push from Okta).
- IP allowlist for staging and prod egress (we will provide subnets).
- A short-lived service account pattern for background jobs that call the Redwood API.

Can you share an implementation checklist and who from your side will own the SAML/SCIM handoff? Also please confirm if Redwood needs any org-level policies or support with IP allowlist testing.

Attaching a short diagram of our identity flow and a list of preliminary IPs.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Cloud Infrastructure, Orion Financial
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@orionfin.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-07T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: SSO + SCIM + IP allowlist for Redwood integration

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Welcome — excited to get Orion onboarded.

Short answer: yes, we can support Okta SAML + SCIM push, IP allowlist testing, and a recommended short-lived service account pattern.

I pulled together the onboarding checklist below and copied Monica (CS lead) to coordinate scheduling and Ben (eng) for the technical handoff. Proposed immediate next steps:

1) Internal kickoff (30 min) to align IdP attributes and SCIM group mapping — propose Thu 2027-04-08 10:00 PT.
2) Provide test Okta metadata (IdP metadata XML + SCIM admin token scope) — Orion to send.
3) Redwood to provide SAML SP metadata and assertion guidance (expected attributes: email, given_name, family_name, groups, role).
4) Run SCIM push in staging with a small group (~5 users) and validate group-to-permission mapping.
5) IP allowlist QA — Orion provides subnets; Redwood will open a test endpoint and confirm egress/IP observations.
6) Service account pattern — Redwood recommends short-lived token exchange via customer-managed KMS and rotating SCIM-provisioned service accounts; we'll draft a runbook.

I attached a one-page checklist and a template SCIM payload we use for onboarding in Drive (link below).

Link: https://drive.example.com/drive/folders/0B_orion_onboard_docs

I will own the overall handoff and schedule; Monica will coordinate CS tasks. Ben, can you pick up the technical items in step 3 and 4?

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-07T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Orion onboarding — tech asks and owners

Team — quick internal note following Alex's request. Please keep replies short so I can forward one consolidated plan back to Orion.

Summary of what Orion needs: SAML SP metadata + attribute mapping guide, SCIM push support and sample payloads, a small staging IP allowlist test, and recommended service-account lifecycle.

Proposed owners:
- Ben: generate SAML SP metadata, validate attribute mapping, stand by for Okta metadata parsing.
- Monica: coordinate staged user list and scheduling with Orion; own CS comms and acceptance criteria.
- Marissa: review compliance items and ensure we capture any SOC2/archivability notes for the service account runbook.

Ben — can you confirm by EOD if we have an off-the-shelf SP metadata file and SCIM example we can share? If not, estimate ETA.

Also: flagging a risky item — Orion wants a short-lived service account pattern that will be used by backend jobs to call Redwood directly. We should avoid long-lived secrets; propose OIDC token exchange with customer KMS. Marissa, can you surface anything that blocks that pattern?

Thanks,
Irene
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@orionfin.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@orionfin.com
Date: 2027-04-08T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: SSO + SCIM + IP allowlist for Redwood integration

Irene / team — thanks. Attached are the Okta IdP metadata XML and a CSV with the subnets we will use for staging (small set) and prod (separate list). Also included is the SCIM admin token request form we filled out.

Attachments: Orion_SSO_Diagram.pdf; SCIM_Token_Request.csv; IP_Allowlist_Subnet_List.txt

For the service account: we can support OIDC token exchange and will provide a short-lived client for staging (TTL 1 hour). For production we are open to rotating keys via our KMS (we use HashiCorp Vault).

We can do the Thu 10:00 PT call. Let us know the calendar invite and dial-in.

— Alex
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-09T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Orion onboarding — tech asks and owners

Quick update for handoff:

- SAML SP metadata: I exported an SP metadata XML (attached to my internal ticket) and created a short attribute mapping doc. Core attributes we require: email (NameID/email), groups (SCIM group claim or groups attribute), given_name, family_name. We also accept custom attributes in the x-redwood-claim namespace if needed.
- SCIM: I validated our SCIM endpoint supports PATCH & bulk POST for groups. I attached a minimal example JSON payload we can paste into the Okta push connector.
- IP allowlist: I opened a temporary test endpoint for Orion staging at https://staging-api.redwood.ai/test-ip-check and recorded accepted egress IPs. For production we'll add the prod subnet range to the firewall rule set after the SCIM/service-account cutover.
- Service accounts: recommend short-lived OIDC exchange. Implementation notes: customer requests service account via SCIM group named redwood-service-accounts; we provision a transient identity with TTL tokens (1h) and rotate via vault/okta if Orion prefers. Marissa — this pattern needs a brief doc for audit trails; I will include logs of service-account tokens to our observability pipeline.

Next steps: Monica, please confirm the staging user list and schedule the Thursday call. I will join and bring the SP metadata + SCIM sample.

Ben
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
